paper_sections.title: The Temporal Dynamics of Voluntary Emotion Regulation
Modulation of the sustained by the immediate aftereffect

description.value: The study investigated whether voluntary emotion regulation by detachment produces immediate and sustained changes in amygdala activation after regulation ends.

design.value: Healthy female volunteers completed two sequenced fMRI tasks: active regulation of aversive visual scenes followed approximately ten minutes later by passive viewing of the same stimuli.

description.value: Used to rule out effects of altered mood states; scores above the cut-off score of 9 led to exclusion.
Used to rule out effects of altered mood states.
Used to rule out deficits in emotion perception.
Used to test whether habitual emotion regulation strategies modulated potential aftereffects.
A measure of habitual thought control used to test whether it modulated potential aftereffects.

description.value: Control experiment rating from 0, weakest, to 7, strongest.

description.value: 20 healthy right-handed female volunteers (24±3 years) without any history of neurological or psychiatric illness participated in the imaging study. Two subjects reached BDI scores above the cut-off score of 9 and thus were discarded from further analyses.

exclusion_criteria.value: history of neurological or psychiatric illness
BDI scores above the cut-off score of 9

medical_condition.value: without any history of neurological or psychiatric illness

diagnostic_instrument.value: Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), State Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20)

clinical_characteristics.value: All 18 subjects included in the analyses had average (non pathological) scores on the BDI, STAI and TAS-20.

task_description.value: Subjects saw 60 pictures of negative or neutral content and either simply watched the pictures and permitted all upcoming emotions or intentionally regulated their emotions by taking the position of a neutral observer. After picture presentation for 8 s, subjects were instructed to not regulate any more and relax for 20 s.

instructions.value: Look at the following picture directly but try to take the position of a noninvolved observer, thinking about the present picture in a neutral way; or Look at the following picture directly and permit feeling your emotions.

stimuli.value: 60 pictures of negative or neutral content taken from the International Affective Picture System.

task_performance_measures.value: emotion regulation success rated post-hoc on a 9-point-Likert scale

task_description.value: Approximately ten minutes after task 1, subjects just looked at the 60 pictures from the IAPS again, presented for only 1 s each in a newly randomized order.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to just look at the 60 pictures from the IAPS again.

stimuli.value: The same 60 negative and neutral IAPS pictures from task 1.

task_description.value: An independent sample used a trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect to confirm the success of emotion regulation.

task_performance_measures.value: trial-by-trial rating of subjective negative affect

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: T2* weighted functional MR images were obtained using event-related echoplanar imaging in a tangential-axial orientation. Image size was 64×64 pixels, with a field of view of 192 mm and flip angle of 90°. In task 1, one whole-brain volume consisted of 31 slices. Slice thickness was 3 mm with 25% gap.

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Siemens Allegra scanner equipped with a head coil

description.value: Task 2 volumes were obtained every 1500 ms. One volume consisted of 23 slices with a slice thickness of 3 mm with 25% gap, covering the brain from the temporal poles to the superior parietal cortex and including the amygdala, prefrontal and parietal cortex. All other acquisition parameters were similar to task 1.

description.value: For each subject, three-dimensional T1 weighted anatomical volumes were acquired.
Data preprocessing and statistical analyses were carried out with SPM 2 and Matlab 6.5.1. Preprocessing included realignment, spatial normalization to the EPI-template and spatial smoothing.

steps.value: spatial normalization to the EPI-template (2×2×2 mm)

model_settings.value: The regression model consisted of 5 regressors—instruction, non-regulated negative, non-regulated neutral, regulated negative, regulated neutral—and six regressors describing residual motion. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by an autoregressive model of 1 order and low frequency drifts were removed via high pass filter.
Second level random effects group analysis using a within-subject ANOVA with a 2×2 design, factors regulation condition and valence, with non-sphericity correction and a t-statistic for every voxel.

level.value: second level random effects group analysis

model_settings.value: Mean amygdala time courses were analyzed with factors valence, regulation and period, using data from scan 5 and scan 9.

Regression analysis on extracted individual data for the contrast regulation negative>no-regulation negative in DLPFC with the contrast no-regulation negative>regulation negative in left and right amygdala.
